label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
On behalf of the organising team, thank you to everyone who made our Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms possible.

We held the school from 5–7 November 2026 in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. We received 112 applications and selected 41 MSc and early PhD participants from nine states, based on a statement and one reference.

My fellow organisers, Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza, and I are grateful to our faculty mentor, Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, for her guidance throughout. Thank you to our speakers: Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) for his lectures on Mordell–Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) for modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined us online from Kraków for computations in Sage.

One moment I’ll remember: an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer’s notes. She corrected it live and thanked him. That exchange captured what we hoped the school would be: a place where students could ask questions and take part.

The second afternoon brought a different challenge. The power was out for nearly two hours and laptops died, so we moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards. It turned out to be my favourite session of the three days.

The problem sessions, led by six PhD student volunteers, worked especially well. Thank you to all six for the preparation and TA work. We hope to keep this format in future editions. Thanks also to Mr. Prakash Salunke, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when a booking went wrong, and to everyone in the office who helped us along the way.

The institute’s student initiative grant of Rs 2.4 lakh supported the school, including hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students. We are grateful for that support, and to all the participants for bringing their questions and energy.

For MSc students especially, small schools can offer something that is harder to find at a large conference: time and space to ask questions. We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to funding. Slides and problem sheets will be shared on the department website within two weeks.
